Our Story

Wren's Story

Wren Jansen was diagnosed with very high-risk Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia at just 3 years old. And suddenly, her family’s life was divided into BC and AD – Before Cancer and After Diagnosis. Before cancer, they had time, wonderful experiences, and promises for memories yet to be made with their soon-to-be family of 6. After diagnosis, cancer took nearly every ounce of their lives and strength, stealing health, sleep, and valuable time. Brandi recalls, “I went from being worried about having 4 children and driving a minivan, to the crushing thought that I might not get to have 4 children. It was a swift shift in perspective.” It has guided everything she has done since.

Wren endured 2 ½ years of harsh chemotherapy by mouth, intramuscularly, via her port, and pumped into her spine and brain, but that was not enough. Due to rare tumors found in the marrow of her skull, Wren also received 10 rounds of radiation therapy to her still-developing 4 year-old brain. Just before Wren got the first of 17 blood and platelet transfusions that would be needed, an amazing nurse at Levine Children’s Hospital recognized her worry and told her the bag of blood was “unicorn juice, because it is magic and will make you feel better.” That resonated and the term “Unicorn Juice” and anything unicorn-related stuck. Unicorns became a symbol of trust, hope, and a little magic.

Watch Wren Tell Her Story

All in for Wren


Thankfully, the Jansen family had a village of friends and family who fought hard with them. Wren was lucky, if there is any luck in cancer. In December 2018, at 6 years old, Wren rang the bell, signaling the end of her treatment with many of her friends and family by her side to celebrate.

During those years spent in the halls of Levine Children’s Hospital in Charlotte, NC, her mother Brandi witnessed many families making impossible choices and facing questions like:


Can I miss another day of work so I can be present for my child’s medical treatment?
Can I afford treatment and medications?
Is there enough gas in my car to make it to the hospital today?
Do I have enough money to feed my family?


Brandi was struck by the realization that, for her family, all they had to do was fight cancer  – but others around her were fighting both life and cancer. Some families missed treatment due to not having enough money to pay for gas or their medications. She also connected with other moms in those hallways and realized that some of them just needed a glimmer of hope, to not feel alone, to remember that they had a village supporting them, even if they couldn’t see it or feel it.

Wren’s Village was created as a 501(c)(3) nonprofit with the goal of supporting families battling pediatric cancer, financially, emotionally and ensuring blood was always available when needed, with the ultimate goal of FUNDING A CURE.





Our Mission

As it’s guiding mission, Wren’s Village aims to provide:

Wren’s Wallets: $250 in gift cards to help with gas, medications, food, some fun, and a lot of hope to ease the unexpected burden that pediatric cancer has on a family, regardless of where they are in their journey.

Funding to support pediatric cancer research. As of 2023, funding for pediatric cancer research totals less than 4% on a national level.

Sparking awareness to action through outreach, education, & blood drives.

It gives them the courage and ability to accept it and have hope for their own child. Thank you again for the love and energy and everything you do to make Wren's Wallets happen. They are such a huge blessing!”
